gates.title: Terminal output is paced by renderer parsing
gates.invariant: A push PTY pauses above the cumulative ACK high-water mark and resumes below the low-water mark.

gates.title: Terminal snapshots restore an absolute cursor
gates.invariant: A serialized terminal screen ends with an absolute cursor position when a cursor is available.

gates.title: Terminal glyph and renderer addons are defensive
gates.invariant: Unicode, link, search, and WebGL addons cannot prevent the DOM renderer from booting.

gates.title: Lens keeps component context with element picks
gates.invariant: A Lens element selection may include a parent-to-leaf React component chain without requiring it for non-React pages.

gates.title: Diff comments can return to the active agent
gates.invariant: A review comment retains its diff line anchor and can be submitted as the next agent prompt.

gates.title: Codex turns expose checkpoint provenance
gates.invariant: A normal Codex turn emits a checkpoint boundary with the current Git ref when available.

gates.title: Provider IPC stays wired end to end
gates.invariant: Every provider preload method has a matching Window API declaration, validated main handler, host protocol request, and host dispatch route.

gates.title: Provider turns have one terminal boundary
gates.invariant: Claude and Codex turns deliver exactly one terminal event and release runtime and pending-decision state after completion, abort, timeout, or process failure.

gates.title: Utility inference remains provider neutral
gates.invariant: Task naming, route classification, and commit suggestions choose an explicit or active provider deterministically and degrade without blocking the primary task.

gates.title: Fleet actions target fresh task identities
gates.invariant: Inline answers, approvals, steering, queueing, and stop actions revalidate project, workspace, task, turn, and request identity before delivery.

gates.title: Task review metrics preserve provenance
gates.invariant: Fleet, Turn Activity, and completion notifications reuse reported or derived task metrics and never present missing checks, usage, or context headroom as zero.

gates.title: Agent platform layers stay distinct
gates.invariant: An automation cannot target an existing task, a wake-up must target one and cannot mint one on either trigger, the supervisor records wake-ups without importing the ledger that records delegated execution, the run ledger never imports execution runtimes, the secondary executor never writes ledger rows, a delegated task survives a restart while an in-turn subagent never does, utility inference stays mechanical, and the work queue assigns one lane per workspace.

gates.title: A delegated-task control never lands on the wrong child
gates.invariant: The delegation link is the only source of child parentage, so a child stays out of workspace-level listings while remaining fully hydrated and openable; every mutating control carries the identity its row was rendered against and is refused with a reason when the delegated task, workspace, attempt, phase, or turn has moved on; a follow-up never inherits permissions; and every refusal carries a sentence the surface can show as-is.

gates.title: A subagent call acts only for its own task, and writers never share a checkout
gates.invariant: Every task turn carries a host-minted caller grant that resolves only while the turn runs; a subagent tool takes the calling task from it, refuses a parentTaskId or workspace naming another task, and refuses a subagent starting subagents of its own; a turn started through stave_run_task never runs with more autonomy than its caller; a writing subagent gets its own worktree unless the same workspace is asked for, which is refused while another writing subagent is live there; read-only subagents run in parallel in the caller's workspace and return their bounded answer inline and in the caller's next turn.

gates.title: A work graph node names a worker, never a call
gates.invariant: Every agent node is keyed from the delegation ledger where Stave owns the child or from provider identity where the provider owns it; a node derived from a bare tool-use id is marked unsteerable and is never offered a per-agent control; per-agent message, interrupt, and stop are gated on a declared runtime capability and refused with a reason when the identity is no longer live; and the graph reducer tolerates late, duplicate, and partial events without inventing an edge.

gates.title: A wake-up never overrides the user
gates.invariant: A due wake-up occurrence defers to an active turn without being consumed, pauses while an approval or question is pending or the task's provider runtime changed, stops with an explicit reason on archive, expiry, or the occurrence cap, catches up at most once after a restart, and records every occurrence idempotently. A completion trigger obeys every one of those rails, consumes each finished delegated run exactly once however many times it is delivered, coalesces a batch into a single wake-up, is capped by default so the wake chain cannot recurse forever, wakes the task on its own provider and model rather than a default, notifies the user when a consumed wake-up produced no turn instead of losing it silently, and stops with 'completion-unobservable' rather than waiting silently when completion cannot be seen.

gates.title: An agent run supervises one task and completes stages only on evidence
gates.invariant: An agent run advances exactly one lead task and never creates a task; a stage completes only through a recorded stage report or a Stave action result, never because a turn ended; a turn that ends without a report is nudged once and then marked stuck, and unreachable reporting blocks instead of nudging; a stage with an external effect the agent run's consent does not list always waits for sign-off; and at most one supervisor entry starts automatic turns on a task at a time, so an agent run pauses its lead task's wake-up with agent-run-active, refuses new wake-ups there, and a task never holds two active agent runs.

gates.title: Tracker credentials never reach the renderer
gates.invariant: A Jira site credential is written only as ciphertext by a vault that fails closed when encryption is unavailable, travels renderer-to-main only, and is never readable back: every tracker IPC reply and public status carries account identity at most, never an email, an API token, or a Crane connector secret, and the preload bridge exposes no getter for any of them.

gates.title: Host turn persistence is bounded and field-scoped
gates.invariant: A host-service turn never loads a task's whole transcript, keeps at most MAX_LOADED_TASK_MESSAGES resident, writes only the messages an event changed, and writes only host-owned shell fields (tasks, activeTaskId, providerSessionByTask, messageCountByTask) so renderer-owned drafts, tabs, layout and information are never overwritten from a stale host copy; quit waits for the renderer's async flush behind a bounded timeout instead of a synchronous IPC write.

gates.title: A saved agent never grants permissions; every run start records its own consent
gates.invariant: Starting an agent run records the user's own permission settings and the agent's check-ins as the run's consent; its turns take permissions from agentRun.consent only (never from a saved agent or saved workflow), and a publish or Stave action stage the consent does not list always waits for sign-off. Only an agent that checks in only when stuck lists its workflow's external-effect stages at start.

gates.title: A saved agent grants no permissions, starts nothing, and a run follows its start snapshot; delegation to an agent only narrows
gates.invariant: An agent config holds only a default permission from a closed list and no approval bypass; compiling never widens it and imports refuse bypass modes, hooks and inline MCP servers. The agent domain in src/lib/agents imports no host, main-process, persistence or process module, so saving or editing an agent cannot start work. Work runs against a snapshot copied at start; edits after the start never change its instructions, tools or content hash. A delegation naming an agent is refused when the agent is not a delegated task or would run wider than the delegating task's agent; work pinned to a commit is refused when HEAD differs. An agent run stage done by another agent is delegated by the lead task, whose provider and instructions never change.

gates.title: Account sign-in identity exposes only an email and a plan
gates.invariant: The sign-in probe runs in Electron main. The only credential file it opens is a Codex auth.json, and only after `codex login status` reports a ChatGPT login; it reads tokens.id_token, copies out the email and plan claims, and drops everything else, so no token, key, path or raw CLI output reaches the reply, the cache, a log or the renderer. Shared setup never links or copies a login, a credential store or a history entry, filters credential-like settings out of the one copied file, and removes on request only what it added.

gates.title: The built renderer loads from the code-cached origin without losing localStorage
gates.invariant: Built renderer assets are served only from inside the renderer directory over the stave-app://renderer scheme, which Chromium may keep V8 code cache for. A profile whose localStorage is still at file:// keeps loading from file:// until every entry has been copied and read back at the new origin; only then is the marker written, and a timed-out or failed copy never writes it.

gates.title: Code-block highlighting stays off the renderer main thread
gates.invariant: Chat code blocks are highlighted by a module worker that loads the same grammar set as the main-thread highlighter. When workers are unavailable, the worker fails to start or its highlighter fails to initialise, every owed and later block is highlighted on the main thread instead of staying plain; an unknown language still rejects so the block renders plain text.

gates.title: The editor runs from the bundled Monaco, never a CDN
gates.invariant: Every module that can mount a Monaco editor waits until the lazily loaded bundled runtime has called loader.config({ monaco }); an editor mounted earlier would make @monaco-editor/react fetch its CDN build. The editor, its diff view and the TypeScript worker work with the network offline.

gates.title: An agent's secret request never carries the value
gates.invariant: stave_request_secret takes only a variable name, a reason and a label under a strict schema, refuses external callers, read-only tasks and reserved names, and resolves to status metadata. The value travels renderer to main only through secret-requests:respond, from a Stave window's main frame, straight into the encrypted vault; the tool result, published request views, IPC replies and the Local MCP request log never contain it, and only the secret id is bound to the task.
